text.p: Shell Oil Co said on Monday investigators were trying to find the cause of an explosion that ripped through a chemical plant and damaged nearby homes.

Shell spokesman Dennis Winkler said company, union and government representatives were combing through the wreckage, but that so far "the cause of the incident and the extent of the damage are unknown."

The blast occurred on Sunday in the plant's olefins unit where chemical feedstocks such as ethylene and propylene are produced. Winkler said the unit was shut down, but that the other parts of the giant complex were still operating.

The explosion touched off a spectacular fire in the plant and sent a large plume of black smoke trailing across the sky. Shell said it had received 73 calls from people whose homes and businesses were damaged by the explosion shockwave.
The company said 30 employees received treatment for cuts and bruises, but none had major injuries.
One worker suffered chest pains and another was bitten by a snake during clean-up operations. Both were taken to a hospital for treatment and later released, the company said.
Shell Oil is a unit of Royal Dutch/Shell Group.
